title: My family
grammar: This is my… / Who is this?

scene.speaker: nico
scene.bubble: Look at my family photo! This is my mum, this is my dad… and oops — Pip is in the photo too!
scene.intro: Nico brings a special photo to school today: his family photo! Look — his mother Rosa with her big smile, his father Juan who is very tall, his little sister, and the baby cousin who is only one. But wait… who is that little black and white bird next to grandma? PIP! He flew into the photo! Who is in YOUR family? In this unit you will learn to say it in English.

activities.title: Read and write the family words.

words.clue: The smallest person in the family.

activities.title: Match the word with the short word.
Listen to Nico. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.script: Astrid: Nico, who is in your photo? … Nico: This is my family! Look, this is my mother. Her name is Rosa. … Astrid: And is this your father? … Nico: Yes! His name is Juan. He is very tall. … Astrid: Have you got brothers and sisters? … Nico: I've got one sister. She is five years old. … Astrid: And who is the baby? … Nico: That's my cousin. He is one year old! … Astrid: And… why is there a bird in the photo? … Nico: Ha! That's Pip! He flew into the photo. Silly Pip!

data.text: Draw your family in one minute (stick people are fine!). Show your partner and say: "This is my mother. This is my brother." Your partner points and asks: "Who is this?"

activities.title: Read about the photo. Write the missing words.

data.text: This is my family photo! My {1} is Rosa and my {2} is Juan. My little {3} is five years old. The {4} is my cousin — he is one!

activities.title: Two family photos! Find the differences.

homework.prompt: Stick or draw a family photo. Write the words with arrows: mother, father, sister… and one full sentence: This is my family.

outcomes.puede: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.
